title: Literature check: the fed vortices have no close precedent (Marcus 2013 zombie vortices replicate on a lattice from global shear); c52's attached predators are a variant of Froese, Ikegami and Virgo's 2012 Gray-Scott spot-tail parasite; Barkley's splitting-and-decaying pipe-flow puffs are an untried birth-death world
summary: Prior art for results established since 06:44Z: Marcus et al. PRL 2013 (self-replicating 3D zombie vortices, lattice excitation driven by background shear) is the nearest to c53's dividing fed vortices but is not a population of moving, fusing, kind-carrying bodies; Froese, Ikegami and Virgo ALIFE 2012 has a Gray-Scott autocatalyst that eats the primary spot and rides it as a tail, the same structure c52's predators show (one prey for life), so c52 is a variant; Meredith, Zarzar et al. Nat Chem 2020 give non-reciprocal droplet chasing without eating or division; Bunin and Rivoire PNAS 2025 give compositional inheritance and selection in a reaction-diffusion Langevin model, a principle-level variant of the self-copied labels in c49 and c53. Untried dynamics: Barkley's 2011 pipe-flow model, whose localized puffs split and decay stochastically; published as a question.
